newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines' MPC H1 net seen jumping 25 percent.
newsitem.headline: Philippines' MPC H1 net seen jumping 25 percent.

text.p: Metro Pacific Corp (MPC) is seen posting a 25 percent rise in net income in the first half of 1997 and the firm would be able to meet its full-year target of 1.1 billion pesos, analysts said on Monday.
But they warned that next year's income could be affected by the company's acquisition of an additional stake in a property project in Fort Bonifacio, the new business district in Manila.

A Reuters poll of six stock brokerages showed Metro Pacific, the local investment arm of the Hong Kong-based First Pacific Co Ltd, was expected to post an average net income of 494.50 million pesos in the six months to June.
The firm reported net income of 393.16 million in the first six months of 1996.
Contributors to the poll expect Metro Pacific to meet its target of 1.1 billion pesos in net income this year, up from 843.9 million in 1996.
Analysts said the main drivers of Metro Pacific's earnings this year would be its cellular phone unit Smart Communications Inc and its property unit Bonifacio Land Corp.
Both firms are together expected to account for 67 percent of Metro Pacific's earnings this year, said Noel Reyes, vice-president for research at Anscor Hagedorn Securities.
"This year (1997) is a transition period for Metro Pacific because of its announcement to increase its stake in both Smart and Bonifacio," Reyes said.
Metro Pacific announced recently it had agreed to buy the 16 percent interest of Filinvest Group in Bonifacio for 5.36 billion pesos.
The buyout raised to 56 percent Metro Pacific's total equity in Bonifacio, comprising 17 private firms which hold 55 percent of Fort Bonifacio Development Corp.
Fort Bonifactio Development is transforming a 214-hectare lot on the edge of Makati into a new business district.
Metro Pacific said its board had agreed to raise its stake in Smart from 28 percent but did not say by how much the stake would be raised.
The acquisition by Metro Pacific of an additional 16 percent stake in Bonifacio would probably be financed through debt and equity, traders said.

"If we assume that it borrows 50 percent of the required amount, using a conservative six percent interest, we estimate that this will increase annual interest expenses by 161 million pesos, thereby diluting earnings per share by .05 pesos," Sapphire Securities said in an advisory to clients on June 30.
